messages.author: b8732c21e549a885
messages.subject: [tidyr] spread function (long format to wide format)
parts:
I am trying to use the spread function to reshape data (long format to wide format).  However, the order of the variable changes after reshaping from the long format to wide. format.  Anyone knows the answer for this?!  Thanks.

Example:

library(dplyr)
stocks <- data.frame(
  time = c(1,3,5,2,4,6,7,8,9,10),
  X = rnorm(10, 0, 1),
  Y = rnorm(10, 0, 2),
  Z = rnorm(10, 0, 4)
)
stocksm <- stocks %>% gather(stock, price, -time)
stocksm %>% spread(time, price)

  stock         1          2         3         4           5         6
1     X  1.571426  0.4254801 -1.496779  1.556063 -0.02754862 0.5580478
2     Y  3.572219  2.2055267 -2.004602 -1.782054  3.13622092 2.4577910
3     Z -1.737320 -1.8457673 -4.907422  3.777605 -2.04690426 5.9274940
           7         8         9          10
1  0.8066553 0.9165995 0.1237089 -0.46649471
2  1.2864357 1.1796152 4.9510654 -0.06040873
3 -3.2505174 5.2893297 5.5685850 -4.07154506

I want the order of variable just like the original data. For example,

   stock 1  3  5  2  4  6  7  8  9  10
1     X
2     Y
3     Z

messages.subject: Re: [tidyr] spread function (long format to wide format)
parts:
Best example I can find is here: 
http://www.rstudio.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/02/data-wrangling-cheatsheet.pdf

dplyr::%>% 
Passes object on left hand side as first argument (or . argument) of function on righthand side. 
x %>% f(y) is the same as f(x, y) 

y %>% f(x, ., z) is the same as f(x, y, z )

I agree that it is not terribly clear what that does in the help. The object previous to the %>% (or semi-deprecated %.%) is substituted into what is after. 

HTH, 
B

As one looks at the first example there,

library(magrittr)
car_data <-
mtcars %>%
subset(hp > 100) %>%
aggregate(. ~ cyl, data = ., FUN = . %>% mean %>% round(2)) %>%
transform(kpl = mpg %>% multiply_by(0.4251)) %>%
print

... it seems to me in the construction:

. %>% some_fun

... is really equivalent to

function(x) some_fun(x)

So I had been thinking that the dot was a data-object, but am now that I should instead be thinking of the combo of dot-pipe as an anonymous local function constructor?

> On Jun 18, 2015, at 11:25 AM, Hadley Wickham wrote:
>
>>>> It's my understanding that '.' in this case represents the product of all the previous steps. In this case your spreading stocksm by time and price and then subsetting that. In most of the dplyr/tidyr functions it is presumed the input is the previous product, but you can specify using '.'.
>>>
>>> So trying to find it in the help system (designed for functions) might be difficult since it's not a function. And it doesn't have an entry in the Index and it's not in the `dplyr-package` help.
>>>
>>> I tried going though several of the HTML sections linked from the vignettes section of dplyr with no useful results. I do see it in the help examples for ?summarise_each. I guess one is supposed to come to this effort from an SQL background and infer that dplyr-"." is analogous to SQL-"*"?
>>
>> It's not a dplyr feature - it's from magrittr:
>> http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/magrittr/vignettes/magrittr.html
>
> As one looks at the first example there,
>
> library(magrittr)
> car_data <-
> mtcars %>%
> subset(hp > 100) %>%
> aggregate(. ~ cyl, data = ., FUN = . %>% mean %>% round(2)) %>%
> transform(kpl = mpg %>% multiply_by(0.4251)) %>%
> print
>
> ... it seems to me in the construction:
>
> . %>% some_fun
>
> ... is really equivalent to
>
> function(x) some_fun(x)
>
> So I had been thinking that the dot was a data-object, but am now that I should instead be thinking of the combo of dot-pipe as an anonymous local function constructor?

Looks like what I was really asking for is found at:

?magrittr::`%>%`

... where is it explained that the meaning of `.` is really context-dependent. When I tried to use my theory about 'dot' being an anonymous-function-constructor it seems that this desired but not exactly what Stefan had designed:

> stocksm %>% spread(time, price) %>% function(x) x[ , c(1, 1+stocksm$time[1:10] )]
Error: Anonymous functions myst be parenthesized

A very useful error message as it turned out:

> stocksm %>% spread(time, price) %>% (function(x) x[ , c(1, 1+stocksm$time[1:10] )])
stock 1 3 5 2 4

>
>
>>
>> Hadley
>>
>> --
>> http://had.co.nz/
>
> David Winsemius
> Alameda, CA, USA
